title: add-rag-federated-dev-proxy-litmus-quickstart
author: Maya Patel
description: Introduce a compact 'Federated Dev Proxy' quickstart that simulates multiple small retrieval indexes and tool endpoints for local RAG/agent development, plus a lightweight litmus telemetry harness to exercise streaming, partial-response resume, and tool-fallback behaviors. Motivation: teams often need to reproduce federated retrieval topologies (micro-index shards, cross-index routing) and flaky tool latencies locally without requiring heavy infra or cloud services; this quickstart gives a repeatable, documented sandbox that fits in a devcontainer. What this PR does: adds the proxy service implementation (Node/TS), a tiny mock index generator (Rust binary compiled in CI), a playground devcontainer with a preseeded compact corpus, a step-by-step quickstart doc for the docs site, and three example agent scenarios (index-fanout, latency-fallback, shard-consistency-eval). Checklist: - [x] Add dev proxy service and local launcher - [x] Add quickstart README and docs site fragment - [x] Add 3 example scenario scripts and sample prompts - [x] Add CI job to build Rust index-generator and smoke the proxy - [x] Add telemetry litmus harness + sample dashboards (Grafana snapshots) - [x] Add integration tests for tool-fallback and partial-response resume Breaking changes: none. Related: ENG-9273 (federated-cache investigation), DOC-421 (authoring quickstarts backlog). Single-line commit summary: "feat(quickstarts/fed-proxy): add federated dev-proxy, index generator, scenarios, docs, and litmus telemetry".

QA_notes: Included a small e2e smoke test that starts the proxy, seeds a 300-doc compact index, runs the index-fanout scenario and asserts top-k results and that tool-fallback fires under induced latency. Runs ~45s locally in devcontainer with defaults.
How_to_run_locally: 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/fed-dev-proxy 2) ./scripts/dev-setup.sh (installs Rust toolchain if needed and npm deps) 3) ./scripts/seed-index --shards 3 4) npm run dev 5) open http://localhost:8080/playground and run scenarios from scenarios/*.json or use curl/SDK examples in the README
